title: Chowdhury & Xu (1995) example 5, embankment on soft clay, circle tangent to y = 5

meta.title: Chowdhury & Xu (1995) example 5, embankment on soft clay, circle tangent to y = 5
meta.notes: As V022a with the circle tangent to the base of the soft clay.

source.derived_from: cSlope verification problem V022b (MIT License), https://github.com/ZilanCiftci/cslope
notes: Fixed circle = cSlope's critical M-P circle among circles tangent to the base of the clay layer (cSlope has no tangent-line search; commercial program B's own circle is not printed), so the comparison is that of two searches within the same circle family.
commercial program B PF 21.39 %, C&X PF 19.733 %. Geometry as commercial program A's Fig. 28.2.
Critical circle (model coordinates): center (40.313, 28.685), R 23.685, tangent to y = 5.

On commercial program A's printed circle (Fig. 28.12: center (40.256, 29.437), R 24.437) cSlope gives Bishop 1.1782 (commercial program A 1.185). The circle grazes the hard layer at y = 5: 0.001 m more radius cuts it and gives 1.43, so the printed radius cannot settle the last 0.6 %.
Chowdhury & Xu's 1.1479 is not checked: it is 2.5 % below both commercial program B (1.178) and commercial program A (1.185, V022b) on this circle family.
cSlope fija options.tolerance = 0.001 (tolerancia del solver) en sus checks; no se importa: ogs usa analysis.tolerance = 1e-05.
